xtmux-lg8.description:
## PROBLEM

Every `sp run executor` dispatched in the xtmux repo since roughly 12:43 local on 2026-07-14 completes in ~8-9s with: 1 turn, 0 tool calls, empty last_output, provider input_tokens=0, and `git.auto_commit result=skipped reason=no_substantive_changes`. The job is marked `done`, NOT `error` — so an orchestrator that only checks status sees a green completion and a silently empty worktree.

Affects BOTH active coordinators, not one bead and not one model:
- xtmux-j46.2 (this session): jobs eb2ba5, 033bbf, c58dbb — on gpt-5.6-luna AND on gpt-5.5.
- xtmux-3ua.2.10 (sibling coordinator, session $2726): jobs at 12:45:46 and 12:46:56, out=0.

Last known-good executor: 12:42:02 on xtmux-3ua.2.6 (out=2460). So the regression window opens ~12:43.

NOT the cause (ruled out):
- Not the model: reproduced on openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna and openai-codex/gpt-5.5.
- Not the backend/auth: `codex exec --model gpt-5.5 'reply PROBE_OK'` works directly (returns PROBE_OK, 17.5k tokens).
- Not the bead: the payload IS built (payload_breakdown shows task_template 2202 tokens + 21 mandatory rules) and the sibling's unrelated bead fails identically.
- Not stale-base: that gate fails loudly with error_code=stale_base; these pass it and then no-op.

Suspicious signal present on every failing run: `[specialist runner] Skipping MANDATORY_RULES injection: rules block too large (2226 tokens, limit 2000)`. Present on the 12:42 SUCCESS too, so likely correlated rather than causal — but it is the only anomaly the runner prints.

## SCRUTINY: critical

A specialist that reports `done` while having done nothing is worse than one that errors: it silently poisons any orchestration loop that gates on status, and both coordinators in this repo are currently dispatching into it.

## SUCCESS

Root cause identified; an empty/no-op specialist turn is reported as `error`, never `done`.

## SCOPE

specialists runtime (~/dev/specialists): the run/turn path and the terminal-status reducer that maps `agent_end` with 0 tools + empty output to COMPLETE.

## NON_GOALS

- Fixing it inside the xtmux repo (wrong repo — this is a specialists runtime bug).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do not paper over it by retrying: three retries reproduced it identically.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Reproduce: dispatch any executor bead and observe 0 tools / empty output.
- [ ] After fix: an empty turn yields status=error, and a real turn yields a diff.

## OUTPUT

Root cause, the status-reducer fix, and confirmation that both coordinators' executors dispatch normally again.
xtmux-lg8.notes:
RECOVERED (transient), but the reporting defect stands.

Outage window: ~12:43 to ~12:55 local, 2026-07-14. Recovery evidence: executor on xtmux-3ua.2.10 succeeded at 12:55:50 with out=4146 on an UNCHANGED bead description, and test-runner on xtmux-3ua.2.11 produced out=2582 at 13:02.

This kills the two hypotheses the sibling coordinator was about to act on: it was not bead content (my j46.2 bead has no nested JSON literal and died identically) and not the model (reproduced on gpt-5.6-luna and gpt-5.5). Transient backend fault.

THE BEAD STAYS OPEN. The transient fault is not the defect worth fixing; the reporting is. A turn that ends with 0 tool calls, empty output and no diff is recorded as status=done, not error. That is what made a 12-minute outage invisible to two coordinators simultaneously and nearly caused: (a) me to close a bead on an empty worktree, (b) the sibling to rewrite a perfectly good bead description and switch models chasing a phantom. Any orchestration loop that gates on status — which is what /using-specialists tells orchestrators to do — is silently poisoned by this.

FIX BELONGS IN: the specialists runtime terminal-status reducer (~/dev/specialists), which maps agent_end to COMPLETE without checking that the turn produced anything. An empty 0-tool turn must terminate as error, so sp ps and the observability DB tell the truth.
